problem: Prior VLN agents, including Recurrent VLN-BERT, encode each view with a single image-level CNN trained on ImageNet or Places. Such a feature is not trained to recognize both the scene descriptions ("bedroom") and the object references ("green chairs") that instructions rely on. Agents initialised from web vision-language pretrained transformers (OSCAR) still feed them image-level scene features rather than the detector region features used in pretraining, which creates a domain shift; naively adding object features to Recurrent VLN-BERT actually slightly hurts performance.
motivation: R2R and RxR train on only 61 environments, so agents cannot learn the long tail of visual landmarks from VLN data alone. Transferring visual grounding from large-scale image-text pretraining is a promising fix, but it only works if the visual inputs match the pretraining inputs, i.e. object detector regions. Instructions use scenes and objects as breadcrumbs, and RxR has about 6 entity references per instruction versus 3.7 in R2R, so an agent that grounds object references should gain most on object-heavy instructions.
key_idea: Feed a Recurrent VLN-BERT (OSCAR-initialised) agent both Places scene features and Faster R-CNN object features. A selective attention mask keeps scene and instruction tokens frozen as context, so only the state and object tokens are updated. Each candidate view is then represented by whichever scene or object token gets the highest state-conditioned attention score (max view aggregation).
insight: Object features only help when the architecture makes processing object-centric like OSCAR pretraining (Table 3). Naively adding them drops val-unseen SR/SPL from 57.90/51.43 to 57.26/50.96. Adding either view aggregation (57.85/51.73) or selective attention (57.73/52.46) reverses the drop, and all three together give 58.71/53.24. Selective attention without object features gives 57.60/52.06. The attention-mask ablation shows the design is specific: 'selective scene attention' (scene tokens as queries) underperforms at 56.83/50.99, and object-only visual input drops sharply to 52.45/46.75, so scenes remain necessary as context. The gain depends on vision-language pretraining: without OSCAR init, SOAT reaches 50.36 SR / 44.69 SPL versus the baseline's 49.21 / 45.53. The gain is largest on RxR instructions with ≥6 object references (+7.91 SR), suggesting improved object grounding.
method: Dual visual encoders: ResNet-152 trained on Places gives one scene feature per candidate view, plus an all-zeros feature for STOP. A bottom-up-attention Faster R-CNN trained on Visual Genome (the same detector used for OSCAR pretraining) gives zero or more region features per candidate view, with redundant detections filtered as in Majumdar et al. 2020.

Recurrent VLN-BERT backbone: an OSCAR-initialised multimodal transformer with a recurrent state token s_t. s_0 is taken from the [CLS] output after encoding the instruction; instruction token outputs ψ(I) are computed once and serve only as keys/values during navigation. The state is updated each step by the Recurrent VLN-BERT refinement: s_{t+1} = [[s_t; F^v ⊙ F^l]W1; a_t]W2.

Selective object attention mask: instruction tokens and scene features V_t are keys/values only and are never updated. The state token and object features G_t act as queries, keys and values, so scenes provide contextual cues for refining object representations, mirroring OSCAR's text+object pretraining setup.

View aggregation: compute state-conditioned scaled dot-product scores ψ(s_t)V_t^T/√d for the unaltered scene features and ψ(s_t)ψ(G_t)^T/√d for the contextualised object features. For each candidate view, the maximum score over its scene and object tokens represents that view.
Action prediction: softmax over the per-view selected scores gives the probability of moving to each navigable nav-graph neighbour or stopping.

Training: fine-tuned with 50% behaviour cloning / 50% RL (policy gradient) rollouts per batch, AdamW, lr 1e-5, batch size 16, 300k iterations on a single TitanX. R2R training is augmented with 1M PREVALENT speaker-generated instructions.

setting.backbone: OSCAR-initialised multimodal transformer in the Recurrent VLN-BERT framework (fine-tuned), with frozen ResNet-152 Places features and bottom-up-attention Faster R-CNN (Visual Genome) region features
setting.training_data: OSCAR web image-text pretraining (initialisation). R2R: 14,025 training pairs plus 1M PREVALENT speaker-augmented instructions. RxR: English subset only (en-IN + en-US), 26,464 training pairs. Fine-tuned with IL+RL.
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 views; candidate views aligned to navigable directions) encoded as Places scene features plus detector object features, with directional features
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (select a navigable candidate or STOP)

numbers_note: The main R2R val-unseen table rounds SR/SPL to 59/53; the ablation tables report the same run as 58.71/53.24. Appendix 3-seed means on R2R val-unseen: Ours TL 11.25±0.08, NE 4.32±0.06, SR 58.01±0.39, SPL 53.37±0.33, versus the reproduced Recurrent VLN-BERT at SR 57.37±0.69, SPL 52.30±0.33. RxR object-heavy analysis subset (354 of 500 randomly sampled val-unseen instructions with ≥6 object references): Ours NE 7.27, SR 41.80, SDTW 32.92, NDTW 52.46; the not-object-heavy subset (146 instructions) gives NE 3.77, SR 61.64, SDTW 53.87, NDTW 69.37. These analysis subsets are not listed as separate entries.
results: R2R val-unseen: SOAT reaches SR 59 / SPL 53, +1.8 SPL over the reproduced OSCAR-init Recurrent VLN-BERT (58/51). R2R test-unseen: SR 58 / SPL 53, versus 58 / 52 for the reproduction. English RxR val-unseen: SR 44.2 / SDTW 36.4 / NDTW 54.8, gains of +3.7 SR, +3.4 SDTW and +2.4 NDTW over the reproduced baseline (40.5/33.0/52.4), and +18.6 SR / +13.5 NDTW over the RxR baseline. On object-heavy RxR instructions the SR gain grows to +7.91 (41.80 vs 33.89). SOAT still trails Recurrent VLN-BERT with PREVALENT initialisation on R2R (val-unseen 63/57, test 63/57).
limitations: Gains on R2R are small (about 1 SPL averaged over 3 seeds), and SOAT remains below Recurrent VLN-BERT with PREVALENT (VLN-specific) pretraining. Val-seen performance drops noticeably versus the baseline (SR 62.78 vs 69.93).

The object detector is trained on web photos from Visual Genome, leaving a domain gap to viewpoint-determined indoor Matterport panoramas. OSCAR pretraining has the same gap, with no VLN-domain pretraining stage.
Evaluated only on English RxR and in the discrete nav-graph setting, not in continuous environments or multilingual RxR. The benefit vanishes without vision-language pretraining.
